title: The Ptolemies
objective: After this level you can explain how a Greek family ruled Egypt for 300 years.
summary: Ptolemy, Alexander’s Macedonian general, founded a dynasty that ruled Egypt for almost 300 years. They appeared as pharaohs on temple walls while keeping their own Greek ways.

cards.headline: For almost 300 years, Egypt’s kings were Macedonian Greeks named Ptolemy.
cards.body: How does a foreign family hold a country that long? By being two kinds of ruler at once.

cards.headline: Ptolemy takes charge
cards.body: When Alexander died in 323 BCE, his Macedonian general Ptolemy became governor of Egypt, and in 305 BCE he proclaimed himself king. His dynasty ruled until 30 BCE. Naming the heirs was easy: the kings ran from Ptolemy I to Ptolemy XV. If you’ve ever lost track of which one is which, you’re in good company.

cards.headline: Two faces of one crown
cards.body: To their Egyptian subjects, the Ptolemies looked like proper pharaohs: they backed Egyptian temples and appeared on temple walls in the traditional pharaonic style. Ptolemy I also promoted Serapis, a god with Egyptian roots and Greek features, whose cult blended both religions. Remember Manetho from Level 9? He wrote his history of Egypt in Greek around 300 BCE, early in Ptolemaic rule.
cards.callout: Pharaohs on the temple walls, Greeks at home

cards.headline: Only one learned Egyptian
cards.body: Behind the temple images, the family kept its own ways. Ptolemy II married his full sister, Arsinoe II, and brother-sister marriage became a feature of the dynasty. And according to the ancient writer Plutarch, of all the Ptolemies only Cleopatra VII took the trouble to learn Egyptian. Nearly three centuries on the throne, and one ruler who could chat with Egyptians in their own language.

questions.prompt: Who founded the Greek dynasty that ruled Egypt until 30 BCE?

options.label: Nectanebo II, the last native king
options.rationale: He was Egyptian and fled in 343 BCE.

options.label: Cambyses II of Persia
options.rationale: He was a Persian conqueror, centuries earlier.

options.label: Piye, king of Kush
options.rationale: He founded Kushite rule in the 8th century BCE.

options.label: Ptolemy, a Macedonian general of Alexander

questions.explanation: Ptolemy became governor of Egypt after Alexander died and proclaimed himself king in 305 BCE.

questions.prompt: Why did the Ptolemies appear on Egyptian temple walls in traditional pharaonic style?

options.label: Greek law required rulers to be carved in stone
options.rationale: It was about how Egyptians saw them.

options.label: To look like proper pharaohs to their Egyptian subjects
Because they were descended from earlier pharaohs
To hide the fact that they spoke Egyptian
options.rationale: Almost none of them learned Egyptian.

questions.explanation: Backing Egyptian temples and appearing as traditional pharaohs made them look like rightful kings to Egyptians.

questions.prompt: Level 9’s Manetho wrote his Greek history of Egypt’s 30 dynasties around 300 BCE. Who ruled Egypt then?

options.label: The Ptolemies, early in their rule

questions.explanation: Ptolemy I became king in 305 BCE, so Manetho wrote early in Ptolemaic rule.
